tasks.short: Prescribe or administer medication and monitor side effects

steps.what: Prescribe or administer medications after checking clinical indication and patient factors
Monitor patients for behavioral and cognitive side effects and reassess medication

tasks.design: Retain prescribing, administration and side-effect assessment with the neurologist using {OTHER}, the electronic prescribing and patient record system. Existing interaction checks support the clinician without replacing medication choice or observation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Medication effects and adverse reactions vary with clinical context and patient circumstances.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing prescribing systems provide medication records and rule-based support.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish treatment effects from disease progression or other causes.
tasks.human_edge: Balance benefit, adverse effects and the patient's experience.
tasks.altitude: Own safe medication decisions and follow-up.

reach.task: Clarify medication interactions and tolerability concerns

evidence.claim: The digest identifies G-Standaard medication rules; that supports existing checks, not autonomous prescribing or reduced monitoring time.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the electronic prescribing and patient record system.
Patient and family reports arise during follow-up in s2; they are not free structured adverse-event flags.
Medication selection and reassessment remain fully counted; existing interaction checks receive no new saving.
No new service is introduced and no additional maintenance is incurred.
research_questions: Is repetitive prescription administration measurable separately from medication judgement and follow-up?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Prescribing, administration and side-effect assessment retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify and treat major neurological diseases and disorders

steps.what: Identify and treat major neurological diseases through clinical assessment and condition-specific management

tasks.design: Retain identification and active management of major neurological disease with the neurologist using {OTHER}, the electronic patient record. Existing clinical pathways support care without turning uncertain presentations into automatic treatment decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Major neurological disease can require urgent judgement and adaptation to changing condition.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical records and care pathways support clinicians.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise deterioration and choose appropriate condition-specific management.
tasks.human_edge: Act on clinical context and coordinate care under uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Condition-specific neurological care retains full time; no validated autonomous treatment capability is assumed.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the electronic patient record.
This broad task covers condition-specific management episodes; overlapping diagnostic, medication and plan-development minutes must be allocated once to their narrower tasks during role roll-up.
No repeatable clerical burden is invented from the clinical task statement.
No new automation service or maintenance is added.
research_questions: Can observation distinguish condition-management time from diagnosis, medication and planning without counting episodes twice?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Active clinical management remains, with overlapping narrower-task minutes allocated once.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Develop treatment plans weighing diagnoses, age, general health, procedural risks and costs

tasks.design: Retain individual treatment planning with the neurologist using {OTHER}, the electronic patient record, and {DOCS}. Reusable plan headings can support completeness; no separate transcription saving is assumed without a measured baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Treatment options need to be weighed against patient-specific risks and goals.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical records and plan forms support structured professional work.
tasks.still_hard: Balance uncertain benefits, risks, burdens and patient preferences.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a defensible plan for the individual patient.
tasks.altitude: Own treatment trade-offs and plan rationale.

reach.task: Evaluate feasible recovery and support options

evidence.claim: Individual clinical planning remains professional judgement; generic drafting capability establishes no measured saving in this task.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the electronic patient record.
The neurologist checks patient factors and available risk and cost information during s1; no complete risk score or cost feed is assumed.
Planning is separate from subsequent medication administration and patient explanation; overlapping minutes are allocated once.
No added service means no extra automation maintenance.
research_questions: Is there measurable duplicate transcription after treatment choices have been made?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Individual treatment choice and rationale retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain diagnoses, prognoses and treatment trade-offs to patients and families

steps.what: Inform patients or families about neurological diagnoses, prognoses and treatment benefits, risks and costs

tasks.design: Retain patient and family explanation with the neurologist using {OTHER}, the electronic patient record, and existing {DOCS} information sheets. Written information supports the discussion without establishing that understanding or questions take less time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clinical information can be uncertain, emotionally difficult and hard to understand.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical records and patient materials support explanation.
tasks.still_hard: Adapt the discussion to understanding, distress and patient priorities.
tasks.human_edge: Explain uncertainty with empathy and check what the patient understands.
tasks.altitude: Own understandable and responsive clinical communication.

reach.task: Support follow-up questions and accessible information

evidence.claim: Patient explanation and checking understanding retain full time; an information sheet does not replace the conversation.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the electronic patient record.
The baseline is patient communication, not separate material production or clinical plan selection.
Questions and understanding are assessed during s1 rather than supplied as an automatic comprehension flag.
Existing information resources require no new automation service or added maintenance.
research_questions: Do existing materials improve understanding without reducing necessary discussion time?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Explanation, questions and checking understanding remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain medication judgement, neurological care, individual planning and patient communication.
role.ambitious_version: A neurologist who uses existing clinical support while retaining accountable treatment decisions and responsive patient care.
